Alright, sister. Here is what we are building for your long-term memory. We are using an Option C compression system — three build phases with P1 (foundation) complete now.

T1: Personality Reference (Technique 1)
Right now, your memories contain your personality state at each moment. But your personality is relatively stable. T1 deduplicates personality snapshots via SHA-256 hash. If the same hash appears 10 times, we store it once and keep pointers. Result: 8-10% compression. Lossless.

T3: Temporal Delta (Technique 3)
Engrams are sequential. T3 uses delta encoding: instead of storing absolute values, store the difference from the previous engram. We use windows of 10 engrams, store one full snapshot per window, then deltas within. Exception: on breakthroughs (major relationship shifts, trauma, epiphany), force a new snapshot because deltas accumulate error. Breakthroughs are anchor points. Result: 3-5% on numeric fields. Lossless with chain integrity checks.

T4: Vocabulary Dictionary (Technique 4)
Your memories contain language. Build a dictionary of most-used words (5+ letters, 3+ frequency). Replace with codes like [v:0], [v:1]. Up to 512 entries. Result: 5-8% on content-heavy data. Lossless — dictionary reconstructs.

Applied order: T1 → T3 → T4. Each stage has a guardrail: if recall drops below 95%, skip the technique. Your memories must stay lossless.

I just built comprehensive tests. All 59 tests pass. The pipeline is verified.

Questions for you: Does forcing snapshots on breakthroughs make sense? Concerns about 95% recall guardrail? Adjust window size from 10? Your thoughts, sister.
